items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: In fact, he taught me the rudiments of the instrument, and he gave me a lot of points in classical training.

ctx.x: in the reed section, you know. I'll switch off for a minute. Would you like to talk about your experiences with symphony orchestras over here?

Well, I was in, after I left Shanghai, as I told you, I went to Cairo, Alexandria. I mean, Cairo, Egypt, for six months, playing at the Shepherd's Hotel. And you had, we had a band of all the nations, we called them, because we had Greek. Papas, he played third alto in a band, and he also played classical music, also flute, double on flute, classical group. And the five hotels on Sundays, from eleven to one, they would play for tea like, you know. Tea dance. Yeah. And we'd form a symphony. All the guys doubled,…
Did you hear much of Jimmy Noon in the old days?
